description: Values on a TransactionRecord's key path that are not what their step reads, on which the Python and TypeScript verifiers must refuse alike. Each case is transaction-record-parties.json's one-round control with one value changed and record_hash resealed (the record_hash cases excepted). A verification method or signature is read by type, never by truthiness: a value that is not a non-empty string names no key, or is no JWS, so that act's signature does not verify; a JWS whose protected header is not a JSON object does not verify either. Verify each record with did_documents (the two parties' documents, as in transaction-record-parties.json) and the case's offer_hashes; both implementations must reach expected_reason (null when it verifies). A string holding a lone surrogate has no UTF-8 encoding and cannot be canonicalized (RFC 8785), so a record carrying one is MALFORMED_RECORD in both; a well-formed surrogate pair canonicalizes as before. A JWS protected header and payload are decoded as strict UTF-8 with no byte-order mark, and a header must be JSON (no NaN or Infinity): the jws_* rows are genuine signatures under such bytes, and each is an invalid signature in both, beside a control that verifies. Each JWS segment is canonical unpadded base64url: only A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '-' and '_', no '=', a length that is not one more than a multiple of four, and zero unused trailing bits. The b64_* rows are genuine signatures over segment text that breaks one of those rules, each an invalid signature in both, beside a control that verifies. The unreadable_* rows keep the control record and change only a signer's DID document, whose public JWK coordinate is not unpadded base64url: such a key cannot be read, so it is unavailable (KEY_NOT_FOUND), and each of these rows carries its own did_documents.

cases.description: record_hash is 7, not resealed: no hash matches it.

cases.name: record_hash_array

cases.name: record_hash_empty
cases.description: record_hash is "", not resealed: no hash matches it.

cases.name: lone_high_surrogate_in_organization_name
cases.description: parties.responder.organization_name, which no signature covers, holds a lone high surrogate (\ud800). The string has no UTF-8 encoding, so the record cannot be canonicalized; record_hash is the one the TypeScript hasher gave before it refused such strings (JSON.stringify writes the lone surrogate as an escape), so the seal itself is no obstacle.

cases.name: lone_low_surrogate_in_subject
cases.description: subject holds a lone low surrogate (\udc00), sealed the same way by that hasher: MALFORMED_RECORD.

cases.name: surrogate_pair_in_organization_name
cases.description: parties.responder.organization_name holds a well-formed surrogate pair (U+1F600), resealed: an astral character canonicalizes as UTF-8 and the record verifies.

cases.name: jws_header_control
cases.description: The offer re-signed under a plain protected header {"alg":"ES256","kid":...} in UTF-8: it verifies.

cases.name: jws_header_bom
cases.description: The offer genuinely signed under a protected header of a UTF-8 byte-order mark and then {"alg":"ES256"}: a JWS segment is strict UTF-8 with no BOM, so the signature is invalid.

cases.name: jws_header_not_utf8
cases.description: The offer genuinely signed under a protected header {"alg":"ES256","x":"<0xFF>"}, whose bytes are not UTF-8: the signature is invalid.

cases.name: jws_header_nan
cases.description: The offer genuinely signed under a protected header {"alg":"ES256","x":NaN}: NaN is not JSON, so the signature is invalid.

cases.name: jws_payload_bom
cases.description: The offer genuinely signed over a payload of a byte-order mark and then the act's hash: the signed payload is not the hash, so the signature is invalid.

cases.name: b64_control
cases.description: The offer re-signed under a canonical header with '-' and '_' in its text: it verifies.

cases.name: b64_header_one_extra_character
cases.description: One stray character after the header text, so its length is one more than a multiple of four. The signature is genuine over that text.

cases.name: b64_header_padding
cases.description: The header text ends in '=' padding. The signature is genuine over that text.

cases.name: b64_header_padding_inside
cases.description: An '=' inside the header text. The signature is genuine over that text.

cases.name: b64_header_star
cases.description: A '*' inside the header text. The signature is genuine over that text.

cases.name: b64_header_space
cases.description: A space inside the header text. The signature is genuine over that text.

cases.name: b64_header_newline
cases.description: A newline inside the header text. The signature is genuine over that text.

cases.name: b64_header_standard_alphabet
cases.description: The header text in the standard alphabet, '+' and '/' for '-' and '_'. The signature is genuine over that text.

cases.name: b64_header_noncanonical_tail
cases.description: The header text's unused trailing bits are not zero: the same bytes, a different text. The signature is genuine over that text.

cases.name: b64_payload_one_extra_character
cases.description: One stray character after the payload text. The signature is genuine over that text.

cases.name: b64_payload_noncanonical_tail
cases.description: The payload text's unused trailing bits are not zero. The signature is genuine over that text.

cases.name: b64_signature_padding
cases.description: The signature text ends in '=' padding. The signature is genuine over that text.

cases.name: b64_signature_noncanonical_tail
cases.description: The signature text's unused trailing bits are not zero. The signature is genuine over that text.

cases.name: b64_aligned_header_one_extra_character
cases.description: One stray character after a header text whose length is a multiple of four, so the length is one more than a multiple of four. The signature is genuine over that text.

cases.name: b64_aligned_header_padding_inside
cases.description: An '=' inside a header text whose length is a multiple of four. The signature is genuine over that text.
